svg.title: Victoria rabbit food, ordinary rules and true emergency gate
svg.desc: A working two-panel decision card. Panel A puts human life first when a person faces an immediate risk of death or really serious injury and an otherwise prohibited act is the only reasonable response. It says this is not blanket permission and that hunger or low food alone is not the threshold. It then summarises ordinary Victorian trapping boundaries and states that the card gives no emergency trapping method. Panel B labels the complete checklist as the ordinary food route, repeats the separate immediate-life-danger boundary, and retains identity, effectiveness, non-target, humane-treatment, poison-history and food-safety limits. The card gives no trap construction, bait, placement, dispatch, cutting or cooking method.
svg.text: RABBIT FOOD — LIFE FIRST, NO SHORTCUT
WORKING CARD · PANEL A OF 2 · VICTORIA
TRUE IMMEDIATE THREAT TO HUMAN LIFE: LIFE FIRST
If an otherwise prohibited act is the only reasonable lifesaving response,
Use the least harmful effective action. Try 000 or SOS only if this will not delay action.
Not blanket permission. Hunger or low food alone is not this threshold.
CONFIDENCE + LIMIT
High for the statutory test and trap categories; Moderate for this short summary.
95% wording estimate only — not legal advice, food safety or survival odds.
THIS CARD GIVES NO EMERGENCY TRAP METHOD
No construction, bait, placement, dispatch, dressing or cooking steps.
ORDINARY RULES — SNARES, DEADFALLS + LEG-HOLDS
Non-kill snares and kill traps need prior approval. A compliant small leg-hold
is rabbit-only, private-land/consent controlled and barred from Crown land.
ORDINARY RULES — CONFINEMENT / CAGE TRAP
Prior land consent · minimise injury and non-target capture · inspect as often as possible.
A legal maximum is not a target · humane killing as soon as reasonably possible.
LIFE-FIRST BOUNDARY ≠ TRAP METHOD · READ PANEL B · NEVER USE DETACHED
CAPTURE IS NOT YET FOOD
WORKING CARD · PANEL B OF 2 · PANEL A CONTROLS
ORDINARY FOOD ROUTE — EVERY CHECK MUST BE YES
One NO or UNKNOWN = DO NOT TRAP USING THIS GUIDE. Not an emergency test.
□ Positive European-rabbit identity — not hare, native animal or pet
□ Ordinary route: exact method lawful; permission or approval held
□ Exact method familiar, dependable, inspectable and safely controlled
□ Safe plan for weather, non-target capture and an injured animal
□ Reviewed humane-dispatch skill and suitable equipment
□ Site baiting and poison-treatment history positively known — unknown = STOP
□ Live capture; no abnormal behaviour, disease sign or chemical concern
□ Hygienic dressing, cooling and cooking can be completed safely
This card supplies none of the missing capture, dispatch or processing methods.
SEPARATE IMMEDIATE LIFE-DANGER CHECK
Only immediate risk of death or really serious injury reaches this branch.
Without delaying action, try 000 or SOS. Use a lawful option that can work in time.
Otherwise: only reasonable, least-harmful action; stop when danger ends.
Not legal permission. This does not unlock a missing trap or food method.
SIGNS ARE NOT PERMISSION OR PLACEMENT
Warrens, dung or grazing marks do not clear species, land, trap or food.
NO CONSTRUCTION · NO PLACEMENT · NO DISPATCH · NOT FIELD-APPROVED
